newsitem.title: GERMANY: DMG says Holzmann forecast misinterpreted.
newsitem.headline: DMG says Holzmann forecast misinterpreted.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfall said on Wednesday its revised results forecast for troubled construction firm Philipp Holzmann AG published on Tuesday had been misinterpreted.
DMG, the research arm of Deutsche Bank, said its increased loss forecast for the firm had been wrongly put down to a worsening of the business position of Holzmann in the last few days.
DMG said the main reason for the revision had been the continuing difficult competitive environment for Holzmann, in particular in east Germany.
DMG stressed that it thought Holzmann's restructuring programme would be successful and Holzmann would probably at least break even in 1996.

On Tuesday DMG said it had increased its 1996 loss per share forecast to 31.10 marks from 13.60 marks and its 1997 loss forecast to 57.20 marks from 1.30 marks. For 1998, DMG said it had slightly lowered its earnings per share outlook to 17 marks from 18 marks.

Shares in Holzmann ended Tuesday bourse trade down 18.50 marks, over four percent, at 367.50 marks on the news of the DMG forecast change and continued to slip on Wednesday ending down 8.50 marks at 359 marks.
